data.one_liner: Query YouTube metadata, streams, playlists, captions, and comments without an API key.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Dart interface to query metadata of YouTube videos, playlists, and channels. It resolves and downloads video streams, extracts closed captions, and fetches comments by parsing raw page content and reverse-engineered AJAX requests.
use_when: You want to fetch YouTube video metadata, captions, or comments without using the official YouTube Data API.
You need to resolve and download YouTube video and audio streams directly.
You are building a custom YouTube downloader or media application in Dart.
avoid_when: You require guaranteed long-term stability against YouTube's frequent internal web page and API changes.
You need an official, supported Google API with explicit quotas and SLAs.
strengths: No YouTube API key or usage quotas required.
Supports metadata, playlists, comments, captions, and various stream qualities (muxed, audio-only, video-only, HLS).
Allows choosing different YouTube clients and custom signature solvers.
weaknesses: Relies on reverse-engineering and parsing raw page content, making it prone to breaking when YouTube updates its site.
Requires manual cleanup by closing the HTTP client to avoid halting the Dart process.

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want an official widget to play standard video files or network video URLs inside your Flutter application rather than extracting raw streams and metadata.
